job.title: Data Platform Engineer

description_sections.prose:
Your role is to build the infrastructure that collects, stores and models everything the company knows about its customers, its machines and itself, and turns it into decisions.

That infrastructure is Cyberdeck: we have rebuilt in our own image every operational software product a company like ours would buy, and run it on our own hardware. Owning the software keeps the data in one estate under one identity model for people and agents.

You will own the stores and the pipelines that fill them, quality and provenance as properties of the pipeline, the entity model beneath it, the time-series and geospatial work the company asks of that data, and the serving layer people and agents read through.

We are looking for data engineers with experience and interest in building and operating production data platforms, information modeling and entity resolution, provenance and data quality, time-series pipelines, and geospatial analysis.
responsibilities: The data estate: stores, schemas and indexes, migrations, query performance, retention and isolation rules
Ingestion pipelines: web enrichment, customer orders, machine telemetry, accounting feeds, idempotent, replayable and backfillable
Data quality: contracts and tests at the boundary, anomaly detection, freshness ranking, stewardship workflows
The canonical entity model: one identity per person, company, design, part, order and machine
Entity resolution: deterministic keys, blocking and scoring, a review queue, and reversible merges
Provenance: source, confidence and history on derived records, and corrections that survive a rerun
Time-series and events: a taxonomy for the floor, downsampling, retention tiers, and reliability metrics

job.title: Agent Infrastructure Engineer

description_sections.prose:
Your role is to build the runtime, the identities and the permissions that let agents work inside the company as colleagues of the people here, and the trust model that keeps them inside it.

Merovingian is the AI side of our internal platform: agents run as emulators with their own identities. Instead of expecting agents to carry the process inside them, we wrote the process down outside them, as code, and made the agent an executor inside it.

The work is distributed systems and security: identities and leases, delivery and supervision, permissions enforced as policy rather than instruction, and the evidence layer behind every call. You will own the execution plane and the design of how agents and people share work.

We are looking for engineers with experience and interest in distributed systems, security and access control, the evaluation and observability of agent systems, runtime or language implementation, and how an organization should be structured.

Identity and the collective: allocated identities, roles as leases, heartbeats and takeover, exactly-once delivery
The permission and trust model: need-to-know scoping, per-tool checks, escalation flows, sandboxing, audit trails
Verification and safety: independent confirmation a write landed, refusal paths, handover to a person
Telemetry and evaluation: event taxonomy, tracing, cost accounting, transcript review, rubrics and offline evaluations
Memory: session context and its lifecycle, notes carried between sessions, retention and visibility rules
Tool interfaces: schemas for context economy, errors an agent can act on, access control
Agent organization design: roles and boundaries, escalation and handoff, supervision of many agents

Hands-on production distributed systems: leases and expiry, idempotency, back-pressure, process supervision and their failure modes
Security and access-control engineering: authentication and authorization, capability scoping, secret handling, sandboxing, audit trails
Comfortable close to a runtime in Rust or another systems language: parsers, interpreters, state machines
Fluent with observability of systems whose output is text: structured events, tracing, cost accounting, evaluations

job.title: Applications Physicist, Materials

description_sections.prose:
Your role is the electromagnetic, thermal and structural design of three-dimensional structures made from our conductors and dielectrics, and the measurements that prove them.

That is metamaterial and metasurface design on an effective-medium description of the stack, antennas, filters and via structures, thermal paths and expansion, and the elastic behavior of a layered composite, each closed on an instrument.

You will own the design rules for what can be built from these materials and the property data the solvers run on, each value carrying its instrument and uncertainty. You say what a formulation has to do because a structure has to.

We are looking for physicists and electrical engineers with experience and interest in computational electromagnetics and the measurement that checks it, metamaterial and effective-medium design, and thermal and structural analysis of layered materials.

Transmission and interconnect: characteristic impedance, coplanar and stripline forms, conductor loss, shielded via geometry
The effective-medium description of the stack: anisotropic permittivity, conductivity and loss with uncertainty bands
Thermal design: conduction paths, heat spreading in the stack, expansion mismatch, and repeated cycling
Structural design of a layered composite: directional stiffness, interlayer adhesion, residual stress and warp
Simulation: full-wave and quasistatic solves, thermal conduction, linear elasticity, parametric sweeps and optimization
Measurement: coupon design, vector network analyzer and TRL calibration, resonator, thermal and mechanical testing
Design rules and property records carrying instrument and uncertainty, and requirements back to materials
requirements: A degree in physics, applied physics, electrical, RF or microwave engineering, or equivalent experience
Hands-on electromagnetic design backed by a full-wave solver: periodic unit cells, S-parameters, far-field transforms
Fluent with vector network analyzer work, TRL calibration and de-embedding, and resonator methods for dielectrics
Working knowledge of thermal and structural analysis: conduction, thermal stress, and layered elastic behavior
The judgment to take a structure that measures differently than it simulated back to its cause
Ready to specify the instruments and coupons this work needs, and to set solves beside readings

job.title: GPU and Numerical Methods Engineer, Continuum Engine

description_sections.prose:
Your role is to build the linear algebra and GPU compute underneath a multiphysics solver stack, and make every solve fast, reproducible and interactive. Continuum Engine is our design and simulation tool: it turns design intent into geometry a production process can build.

The numerical side is matrix-free operators, Krylov methods and preconditioning, mixed precision and deterministic reductions. The compute side is Vulkan kernels, memory layout and occupancy judged against a roofline.

You will own the solver substrate and the performance floor: one substrate electromagnetics, conduction and elasticity share, the benchmarks that keep it from eroding, the fidelity tiers and warm sessions that keep the loop interactive, and the reproducibility guarantee every result rests on.

We are looking for computer scientists, computational scientists and applied mathematicians with experience and interest in sparse and iterative linear algebra, preconditioning and multigrid, GPU kernel performance, and numerical reproducibility.
responsibilities: Matrix-free operators for symmetric positive definite systems, reused across physics families rather than cloned
Krylov solvers and preconditioning: conjugate gradient, diagonal scaling through multigrid and deflation, spectrum analysis
Convergence discipline: true relative residual stopping and refusal to return an unconverged solve
Mixed precision: single-precision compute with a double-precision cross-check, and error accumulation over long runs
Reproducibility: deterministic fixed-order reductions, bitwise-identical results across devices, solution signatures, regression tests
GPU compute: Vulkan compute shaders and SPIR-V pipelines, descriptor and buffer layout, occupancy, synchronization
Performance engineering: roofline and bandwidth analysis, profiling, tiling and memory layout, benchmarks in regression
Interactive tiers and distributed execution: preview, refine and full solves, warm sessions, remote accelerators
requirements: A degree in computer science, computational science, applied mathematics or a related field, or equivalent experience
Hands-on writing and tuning GPU compute kernels in Vulkan, CUDA or HIP for numerical workloads
Fluent with sparse and iterative linear algebra, and able to explain why a solver stalled
Comfortable in modern C++ inside a large codebase, and with the floating-point behavior underneath it
The judgment to take a slow kernel back to its cause with a profiler and roofline
Ready to build the substrate every physics family sits on, and write it to be extended
Comfortable working on-site
Bonus: multigrid or domain decomposition, deterministic parallel reductions, mixed-precision refinement, or distributed accelerator execution

The solver work spans the full-wave and quasistatic regimes, the sub-cell and boundary treatments that keep them accurate, and the material and process data model they run on, where every property carries its provenance and uncertainty.

You will own the verification and validation program, from analytic and manufactured solutions to comparison against measured parts, and the data model alongside our materials team, so that a design is judged against the physics of what will be built.

Domain truncation: perfectly matched layers, radiation and periodic boundaries, and the error each introduces
Grids: graded tensor-product grids, adaptive refinement, and quantization of geometry onto the grid
Verification: convergence studies, a posteriori error estimation, manufactured solutions, independent reference solvers in regression
Material and process data: values from nominal to measured, with conditions and uncertainty carried
Homogenization and uncertainty: effective tensors for deposited microstructure, anisotropy, and process tolerance reported separately

Hands-on discretizing and solving partial differential equations in production code, with the numerical analysis behind it
Fluent with convergence studies, manufactured solutions and reference comparisons, and able to say where error originates

job.title: Application Engineer

description_sections.prose:
Your role is to take customers' board designs into build and to be the technical bridge between their engineers and ours, at the level where a requirement becomes a property a material has to hold.

The work is design review and redesign against what the process holds, signal and power integrity, RF and microwave passive design, and the coupon measurement that turns each of those into a rule.

You will own the design rules and the coupon block that rides every board, set the acceptance criteria first-article review runs against, and be the engineer the customer talks to from feasibility through delivery.

We are looking for electrical, RF or microwave engineers with experience and interest in multi-layer stack-up and controlled impedance, passive design backed by full-wave simulation, and measurement that others design against.
responsibilities: Buildability review of Gerber, KiCad and Altium designs against the process, stack-up and clearances
Redesign for embedded passives, three-dimensional conductor geometry, shaped dielectric, and rigid and flex sections
Design rules from measurement: trace and space, current capacity, via resistance, creepage and clearance
Signal and power integrity: controlled impedance, return paths, differential pairs, crosstalk, conductor loss, decoupling
RF and microwave passives: patch antennas, arrays and feeds, multilayer filters, transitions, frequency-selective surfaces
Full-wave and circuit simulation: unit-cell sweeps, far-field patterns, S-parameter extraction, correlation against measurement
Measurement: coupon design, four-wire resistance and LCR, vector network analyzer with TRL calibration, fixturing
First article and customer relationship: acceptance criteria, feasibility conversations, requirements fed back to materials
requirements: A degree in electrical, electronic, RF or microwave engineering, or applied physics, or equivalent experience
Hands-on multi-layer board design in a commercial EDA tool, owning stack-up and controlled impedance through release
RF or microwave passive design backed by full-wave simulation: antennas, filters, transmission lines, matching networks
Fluent with vector network analyzer work, time-domain reflectometry, and the calibration and de-embedding behind them
The judgment to take a structure that measures differently than it simulated back to its cause
Ready to write design rules from your own measurements and to talk to customers directly
Comfortable working on-site
Bonus: rigid-flex design, built-in passive elements, metamaterial structures, or aerospace and defense applications work

job.title: Materials Engineer

description_sections.prose:
Your role is to formulate, characterize and scale the functional materials Nebula uses: silver nanoparticle dispersions, copper metal-organic precursor solutions, and UV-curable acrylate resins.

The work runs on two sides: particle synthesis and colloidal chemistry on the metals, photopolymer formulation on the resins, and on both the rheology, characterization and qualification that decide whether a formulation survives service.

You will help establish this materials group, design its wet lab from the first bench, and run the relationships with local research organizations whose instruments we use until we have our own.

We are looking for materials scientists and chemists with experience and interest in nanoparticle synthesis and colloidal dispersions, photopolymer formulation, and the structure-property-processing work that connects a recipe to a measured result.
responsibilities: Synthesis of silver nanoparticle dispersions and copper metal-organic precursor solutions: reduction, capping, purification, stability
UV-curable acrylate resins: monomers, oligomers, photoinitiators, cure kinetics, glass transition, dielectric constant and loss
Bringing each formulation into its rheological window: viscosity, surface tension and particle size distribution
Sintering and cure studies: densification, resistivity, conversion, crosslink density, adhesion and expansion mismatch
Characterization: DLS and zeta potential, rheometry, DSC, TGA, FTIR, four point probe, SEM, XRD
Qualification against thermal cycling, humidity and electrical stress
Standing up a wet lab: fume hoods, inert handling, purification equipment, methods, safety, suppliers
Collaborations with local research organizations for electron microscopy, X-ray methods and thermal analysis
requirements: A degree in materials science, chemistry, polymer science or a related field, or equivalent experience
Hands-on formulation of nanoparticle dispersions or photopolymer resins, including stability over time and rheology
Fluent with the characterization above and able to explain a result, not just record it
The judgment to diagnose a formulation failure from the data instead of guessing at it
Ready to help build a lab from an empty bench: instruments, methods, safety and suppliers
Comfortable working on-site
Bonus: metal-organic decomposition chemistry, photoinitiator design, laser sintering, or tailoring a material to a deposition process
